propositions: Current clarity measure awards points for volume and legacy shape (H2 headings, character count thresholds, dash bullets) rather than enforcing the documented plan-writing guidance contract for required sections and substantive content.

Clarity-score computation is duplicated across _engine_support/gates.py and llm/plan_review/det_floor.py with inconsistent drift risk, and does not leverage deterministic structural validation that could be shared.

The documented plan-writing guide requires nonempty Context/Problem, grounded Approach/Scope for leaves, child decomposition for containers, and per-AC proof linking, but these are not mechanically enforced as deterministic gates.

Author-guide and criteria-guide conflict on rejected-alternative language and Success Criteria vs. Acceptance Criteria terminology, creating ambiguity for deterministic rule-writing until those conflicts are resolved.

Seven mechanically testable additions are feasible without semantic judgment: required-section shape keyed on graph altitude, per-AC verification coverage with proof-clause parsing, placeholder-word detection in Scope/Approach, grounded file_impact for leaves, AC-item text hygiene flags, Testing shape markers (happy-path and failure cases), and nonempty structural sections.

Recommended scoring should derive compatibility from per-check evidence (satisfied/applicable checks) rather than accumulating points, to prevent filler content from compensating for missing required sections.
